headline: Wall Street closed higher on chips; bitcoin hovers just under $80,000
summary: U.S. stocks closed higher on a chip and Tesla rebound: the S&P 500 rose 0.7% to 7,677, the Nasdaq 0.8% to 26,169 and the TSX 0.4% to 35,944, while Meta (-1.9%), Apple and Alphabet (both -1.1%) lagged and Brazil's market crashed about 15% after Lula's re-election. Crypto sat the rally out: bitcoin is about $79,900 (down 0.6% over 24 hours), ether about $2,306 (down 1.5%), the total crypto market is down 2.5% at $2.69 trillion, and small-cap AI token Quack AI more than doubled in a day. U.S. oil is down about 2% at roughly $101.25, gold is up 0.6% near $4,031 and the 10-year yield held near 4.99%, with Wednesday's Fed and Bank of Canada decisions and Big Tech earnings next.

crypto.label: Cautious
crypto.why: Bitcoin is stuck just under $80,000 and Fear & Greed sits at a neutral 50, but ETF buyers pulled about $774 million late last week, the total market is down 2.5% today and crypto stocks fell while the Nasdaq rallied; gains are limited to small, speculative tokens.

stocks.label: Risk-on
stocks.why: The Nasdaq closed up 0.8% on a broad chip rebound and the VIX fell about 5% to 18.4, but a 10-year yield near 5%, a roughly 15% crash in Brazilian stocks and Wednesday's Fed decision keep the rally on a short leash.

drivers.detail: Meta launched a $35 billion stock sale (about $22.5 billion of common shares plus $12.5 billion of mandatory convertible preferred), per its SEC filing, and Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom signalled interest in buying up to $5 billion, per AP. AMD (+2.8%), Nvidia (+2.4%) and Broadcom (+2.3%) led the rebound into the close, while Meta fell 1.9% to about $631.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Down 0.6% over 24h and 2.5% this week, at about $79,900 (down 5.1% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitcoin fell nearly 2% to about $79,800 in Asian trading Monday as traders cut risk before Wednesday's Fed decision, where any hint of a December rate hike would tighten the money flowing into risky assets, per CoinDesk. It climbed back above $80,000 late in the morning as U.S. stocks rallied, but slipped back just under $80,000 in the afternoon and stayed there even as stocks closed higher. Spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold the coin for stock-market investors) lost about $774 million on Thursday and Friday, per crypto.news, so buying demand from big investors has yet to return.
crypto.meaning: Glassnode estimates ETF buyers and corporate treasuries bought, on average, between about $80,000 and $81,500, so bitcoin is sitting just below the price where many big holders break even; staying under it can prompt more selling. Bitcoin is also failing to keep up with stocks today, a sign that crypto-specific demand is weak right now.

outlook.bullCase: A calm Fed on Oct. 28, ETF inflows returning and a U.S.–Iran deal could lift it back above $82,000–$82,500 (Thursday's lost floor), putting $85,000–$87,000 back in view.
outlook.bearCase: A daily close below $79,000, more ETF outflows, a hawkish Fed or a U.S. strike on Iran could extend the slide toward $77,600 (Glassnode's estimate of the average holder's cost) and then $75,000.
outlook.watch: Whether it closes the day above $79,000, Monday's ETF flow data, the Fed decision and Warsh press conference on Oct. 28, and about $11 billion of bitcoin options expiring Oct. 30.

crypto.name: Ethereum
crypto.move: Down 1.5% over 24h and 3.7% this week, at about $2,306 (down 14% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ether fell nearly 3% to just above $2,300 in Asian trading Monday, per CoinDesk, and is about $2,313 in the late afternoon, down about 1.6% over 24 hours, after a brief late-morning bounce faded. It is still under the $2,400 level that had supported it for about a week, and it led liquidations (forced closures of borrowed bets) over the past day.
crypto.meaning: Ether is lagging bitcoin because big investors keep pulling money from the ETFs. Until those flows turn, rallies may be harder to sustain.

outlook.bullCase: Climbing back above $2,400, with ETF outflows stopping, could open a move toward $2,500 and then about $2,700, where October began.
outlook.bearCase: A break below $2,290 (Saturday's low) with continued ETF outflows and more forced selling could send it toward $2,150–$2,200, and a broader risk-off turn could push it lower.
outlook.watch: Daily ether ETF flows, the $2,300 and $2,400 levels, the ETH/BTC ratio, and any new Glamsterdam upgrade timeline.

crypto.name: Quack AI
crypto.move: Up about 144% in 24h to roughly $0.143 (about 27% in the last hour alone), but only flat for the week after a steep mid-week crash
crypto.why: Quack AI pitches itself as an AI layer for crypto governance, using software agents to read and vote on project proposals across blockchains; its Q token runs on BNB Chain and Ethereum. It ran up about 450% in the week to Oct. 19, reaching about $0.17, then gave most of that back during the week before more than doubling again today; we could not find a specific news trigger, and trader posts credit momentum and futures speculation. It is now the top gainer in CoinGecko's top 100 and trending, with a market value near $665 million.
crypto.meaning: This is a momentum-driven, highly speculative token: a move of more than 100% in a day with no clear news usually reflects traders chasing price, often with borrowed money in futures markets, and can reverse just as fast. Only about 4 billion of the 10 billion tokens are circulating, so later unlocks (tokens released to insiders or funds) could add selling pressure.

outlook.bullCase: If buying keeps up and Q holds above about $0.14, a retest of the Oct. 19 peak near $0.17–$0.18 is possible; a clean break above that would open talk of $0.20.
outlook.bearCase: If momentum traders take profits, Q could quickly drop back toward $0.10–$0.12, and a full unwind of today's spike would put it near $0.06, where it sat before the jump.
outlook.watch: Whether $0.14 holds, futures open interest and funding (signs of leveraged betting), large transfers to exchanges, and any actual product or listing news.

crypto.name: Bitway
crypto.move: Down 32% in 24h and 42% this week, at about $1.14, after an afternoon bounce from near $1.00 faded
crypto.why: Bitway is still the worst performer in CoinGecko's top 100 today, with no specific news trigger we could find; it had already fallen about 25% on Oct. 15 when a hot U.S. inflation report hit crypto, and slid from above $2.60 to about $1.70 in the week to Oct. 24, per CoinMarketCap's update page. Trackers say the top 100 wallets hold almost all of the supply, which makes sharp moves like this more likely, and about 101.6 million BTW (roughly 1% of the 10 billion total, about $115 million at today's price) is due to unlock on Nov. 2, per CryptoTicker. An unlock is when tokens held back for insiders or ecosystem funds become free to sell. An early-afternoon bounce of nearly 30% off a low near $1.00 has mostly faded, typical of a thinly traded token after a crash, again with no news we could find.
crypto.meaning: This is a high-risk token whose price can swing tens of percent in a day, with conflicting public data on how many tokens are actually circulating. Holders face more supply coming each month through 2030, and whether the Nov. 2 tranche goes to early backers (more likely to sell) or ecosystem pools is disputed between trackers.

outlook.bullCase: If selling exhausts near $1.00 and the market absorbs the Nov. 2 unlock without a fresh drop, a rebound toward $1.40–$1.70 (last week's levels) is possible.
outlook.bearCase: If large holders keep selling into thin trading, a break below $1.00 could open a slide toward $0.80, especially around the Nov. 2 unlock.
outlook.watch: Whether $1.00 holds, large wallet transfers to exchanges, trading volume, and price action around the Nov. 2 08:00 UTC unlock.

crypto.name: LayerZero
crypto.move: Down 8.3% in 24h and 15% this week, to about $1.62, off a 24-hour high near $1.79 (flat over 30 days)
crypto.why: LayerZero runs a messaging system that lets apps send tokens and data between different blockchains, and ZRO is its token. It is one of the worst performers in the top 100 today, but we found no fresh headline behind Monday's drop. It has been weak since an Oct. 20 token unlock (about 6% of supply), after which roughly 9.7 million ZRO was reportedly moved to big exchanges, per CoinMarketCap's AI news summary; an unlock is when tokens held back for insiders become free to sell. The project announced on Oct. 20 that its Zero mainnet and lzATLAS launch, which adds a buy-and-burn of ZRO funded by fees, is planned for Nov. 30, per TokenPost.
crypto.meaning: Recurring unlocks keep adding supply that early holders can sell, which has outweighed upgrade news so far this month. The Nov. 30 launch is the project's main potential catalyst, but a fee-funded burn only helps the price if the network earns meaningful fees.

outlook.bullCase: If selling from the unlock runs out and bitcoin steadies above $80,000, ZRO could bounce back toward $1.80–$2.00, where it traded last week.
outlook.bearCase: Continued exchange deposits from large wallets or a weaker crypto market after the Fed could push it below $1.60 toward about $1.40–$1.50.
outlook.watch: Large ZRO transfers to exchanges, whether $1.60 holds, the next monthly unlock date, and any update on the Nov. 30 Zero mainnet launch.

crypto.name: XRP
crypto.move: Down 0.7% over 24h and 0.9% this week, at about $1.29 (down 15% over 30 days)
crypto.why: XRP has held up better than most large coins over the past few days. CoinDesk reported Saturday that Franklin Templeton on Thursday put about $150 million more of its tokenized money-market fund (sgBENJI, a fund whose shares exist as tokens on a blockchain) onto the XRP Ledger, taking the fund's holdings there to nearly 193 million shares, worth roughly $200 million. All of the new shares sit in a single wallet linked to Franklin's issuing account, and it is not clear whether they belong to one investor or several.
crypto.meaning: A big asset manager using the XRP Ledger for tokenized funds supports the network's case for real-world finance, but the fund tokens don't require anyone to buy XRP, so the price link is indirect. XRP is still down about 14% over the past month, so this is a small bounce inside a larger slide.

outlook.bullCase: More tokenized-fund news and a steadier bitcoin above $80,000 could lift XRP back toward $1.40–$1.45.
outlook.bearCase: If bitcoin loses $80,000 again or the wider market turns risk-off after the Fed, XRP could slip back toward $1.20–$1.25.
outlook.watch: Whether Franklin clarifies who holds the new fund shares, bitcoin's hold on $80,000, and the Oct. 28 Fed decision.

crypto.name: Quant
crypto.move: Up 5.0% in 24h and 4.1% this week, to about $201 (up 64% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Quant makes software (its Overledger platform) that lets banks move tokenized money, meaning bank deposits recorded on a blockchain-style ledger, between different systems. The token is up about 70% over the past month after The Clearing House, the payments company owned by big U.S. banks, picked Quant's technology in late September for a project to settle tokenized deposits over its existing payment rails, with rollout targeted for the first half of 2027; seven big UK banks also made the first live customer payments with tokenized sterling on infrastructure Quant built, per CoinMarketCap. It is among the top gainers in the top 100 over the latest 24 hours, and we could not find a fresh announcement behind Monday's jump.
crypto.meaning: QNT is trading on a real business story, bank adoption of tokenized money, rather than pure hype, but the actual rollout is still more than six months away and banks paying for software does not automatically mean demand for the token. After a roughly 70% gain in a month, much of the good news may already be in the price.

outlook.bullCase: More bank or payments-network announcements, or a broader recovery in crypto, could carry it past about $210–$225 on continued momentum.
outlook.bearCase: Profit-taking after a roughly 70% monthly gain, or a wider crypto sell-off if bitcoin loses $80,000, could pull it back toward the $175–$180 area or lower.
outlook.watch: Any new partnership news from The Clearing House or UK banks, whether trading volume stays high, and bitcoin's direction around the Fed decision.

crypto.name: MemeCore
crypto.move: Up 1.3% in 24h and 32% this week, at about $0.95 (down 22% over 30 days)
crypto.why: MemeCore, a blockchain built around meme coins, was the biggest decliner among about 90 large coins tracked by TokenPost on Sunday morning, falling to about $0.92; it has since rebounded to about $0.95 (up about 1.8% over 24 hours), with no specific trigger reported either way. outlook.bullCase: If the sell-off was one large holder exiting and the broader market steadies, it could rebound toward $1.05–$1.15, where it traded earlier this week.
outlook.bearCase: More large-wallet selling or selling ahead of the Nov. 1 unlock could push it toward $0.75–$0.80, its lows from mid-October.
outlook.watch: Large transfers to exchanges from top wallets, the Nov. 1 unlock, and whether the project explains the drop.

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Up 1.1% in 24h and 8.8% this week, at about $1,223 (down 22% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Traders had been positioning for the NU7 upgrade, which developers scheduled for about 7:50 p.m. ET on Nov. 5; it cuts block times from 75 to 25 seconds and sends 60% of fees to a reserve. Futures open interest (the value of open bets) had risen about 19–24% and two large traders reportedly opened about $37.6 million of 10x leveraged longs. Those leveraged bets have been unwinding: CoinDesk flagged ZEC among the coins where bullish traders were closing positions, and it noted an 8% drop in open interest Friday. After dipping below the $1,190–$1,230 support area, the price has bounced back to about $1,224 (up about 0.4% over 24 hours), inside that zone.
crypto.meaning: Much of this month's rally was driven by borrowed money, and this week shows how fast that can reverse. Upgrade dates often bring 'buy the rumour, sell the news' behaviour, so swings both ways are likely into Nov. 5.

outlook.bullCase: Holding the $1,180–$1,200 area and renewed interest as the upgrade nears could bring it back to the $1,375 resistance and, beyond that, the September high near $1,700.
outlook.bearCase: Losing $1,180 would erase the October breakout and could send it toward about $1,000–$1,120, near its 50-day average.
outlook.watch: The $1,180 level, funding rates and open interest, ETF flows, and any upgrade delay.

crypto.name: Solana
crypto.move: Down 1.2% in 24h and 3.6% this week, at about $100.30 (down 17% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Solana completed its Alpenglow upgrade, a major overhaul aimed at much faster transaction finality (the point at which a payment can't be reversed), according to CoinDesk. The price has moved with the market rather than rallying on the news, and it slipped under $100 Saturday morning as bitcoin's break below $80,000 triggered forced selling across crypto, briefly tested $100 again in Asian trading Monday, and it is about $100.20 in the late afternoon, barely above that line.
crypto.meaning: A smooth Alpenglow launch is a meaningful technical milestone, but the market is treating it as already expected. The first days after a big upgrade are when problems usually show up, so stability matters more than headlines.

outlook.bullCase: A trouble-free upgrade and stronger crypto risk appetite could lift SOL back toward $115–$120.
outlook.bearCase: Any outage or bug after the upgrade, or bitcoin staying below $80,000, could push SOL toward $90.
outlook.watch: Whether SOL regains $100, network stability after Alpenglow, bitcoin's $80,000 level, and Solana ETF flows.

stocks.name: Verizon
stocks.move: Fell in Monday trading despite an earnings beat (down about 2.8% in early afternoon, per AP; our live feed does not track VZ)
stocks.why: Verizon reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.31 a share at 7 a.m., above the roughly $1.27–$1.28 analysts expected, and added 406,000 net postpaid phone subscribers (monthly-bill phone customers), its best in years. Revenue of $34.3 billion, up 1.5%, came in below the roughly $34.8 billion forecast, and AP says that miss is why shares fell after rising before the bell. It raised its 2026 outlook for subscriber additions (now 1.1–1.2 million), adjusted earnings ($5.04–$5.06 a share) and free cash flow growth (about 12%), and a report says it signed an AI infrastructure deal with Amazon Web Services worth more than $2 billion.
stocks.meaning: The results suggest Verizon's turnaround in customer growth is real, which supports its dividend (a yield above 6%). The overhang is SpaceX's push toward becoming a fourth carrier, which knocked telecom stocks down sharply this month, so strong numbers may not fully lift the stock while that threat is unresolved.

outlook.bullCase: If the earnings beat and raised guidance hold up through the call and the open, a daily close above about $45.70 (its moving averages) could open the way toward $48.
outlook.bearCase: If investors focus on the revenue miss, or SpaceX signs tower deals, the stock could slip back below $43.07 support toward about $40.30.
outlook.watch: Whether it recovers Friday's $44.66 close, management's comments on competition and SpaceX, any signed SpaceX tower leases, and AT&T and T-Mobile reactions.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.move: Closed down 1.9% at about $631, near the day's low of $628; down about 10% since Wednesday
stocks.why: Meta launched a $35 billion share sale Monday to pay for AI data centres: about $22.5 billion of common stock sold through forward agreements and $12.5 billion of three-year mandatory convertible preferred shares (which turn into common stock later), plus a planned program of up to $60 billion of non-voting Class C shares starting in early 2027, per ZeroHedge and KuCoin News. Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom indicated interest in buying up to $5 billion. Shares rose before the bell, fell to about $629 after the open, recovered to about $648, before closing near the day's low at about $631. Last week's results beat forecasts, but the $135–$145 billion spending plan, roughly -$2.1 billion of free cash flow and a $9.9 billion legal charge sank the stock 7% Thursday.
stocks.meaning: Selling new shares spreads the company's profits over more stock (dilution), and the scale here is unusual for a company that was buying back shares. Chip-maker interest shows suppliers want to keep Meta spending, but it also feeds 'circular financing' worries, where AI buyers and sellers fund each other.

outlook.bullCase: If the offering is absorbed smoothly and investors refocus on 26% revenue growth, it could recover toward $680–$700.
outlook.bearCase: Pressure from new supply, rising credit-risk pricing (its five-year credit default swaps are about double August's level, per ZeroHedge) or weak results from other Big Tech spenders could push it below $630 toward $600.
outlook.watch: The offering's final pricing, whether $630 holds, and Alphabet's and Microsoft's spending plans on Oct. 28.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.move: Closed up 5.2% at about $392, a more-than-three-month high; still about 21% below its 52-week high
stocks.why: Barclays upgraded Tesla to overweight (a buy rating) from equal-weight and raised its target to $450 from $370, citing a widely expected combination with SpaceX that it says should come at a premium, an improving core car business and early signs of a robotaxi breakthrough, per Investing.com. Mizuho raised its target to $460. Trackers counted about 1,250 Cybercab robotaxi sightings around Austin's Formula 1 race, mostly driverless, and the Berlin plant set a weekly record of 7,000 Model Ys.
stocks.meaning: Most of the move rests on a SpaceX merger and robotaxi hopes rather than current car profits, which fell sharply last quarter. That makes the stock very sensitive to any merger news either way.

outlook.bullCase: Concrete merger terms or a smooth Cybercab expansion could carry it toward $410–$420 and then analyst targets around $450.
outlook.bearCase: If merger talk stalls or the gain fades like last week's early jump, it could slip back toward $372 (Friday's close) or $355–$365.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds above $385 through the day, merger committee news, and the NHTSA Cybercab response due Oct. 30.
